title: China’s president says AI should be a team sport, not a solo race
summary:
Imagine if only one kid in your class got to use the coolest new app, and everyone else was left out. That’s kind of what China’s president, Xi Jinping, says is happening with artificial intelligence — AI for short. He says AI should be like a symphony, where lots of countries play together, not a solo performance by just one country.

Xi was speaking Friday at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai, a huge meeting where companies show off their smartest robots and computer brains. He criticized the United States for blocking China from getting some advanced AI chips and technology, calling it “overstretching” the idea of national security.

But Xi didn’t just complain — he also promised to share. China will give 30 countries access to a Chinese-made AI weather warning system, and over the next five years, it will offer 5,000 AI training spots to people from developing countries. That’s like inviting 5,000 kids to a free coding camp!

China also launched a new group called the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, with 29 countries signing up, including Pakistan, Russia, and Kazakhstan. Experts say it’s China’s answer to a U.S.-led AI club called Pax Silica.

Meanwhile, Chinese companies are racing ahead. A startup called Moonshot just released an AI model named Kimi K3 with 2.8 trillion parameters — that’s a measure of how brainy it is. Another famous Chinese AI, DeepSeek, is popular in many countries because it’s open-source and cheaper than American versions. The AI battle is heating up, and Xi wants to make sure China isn’t left on the bench.
why_it_matters: The way AI is developed now could decide what robots and apps you'll use when you grow up, and whether everyone gets a fair chance to learn about them.

background_read: China and the United States are in a fierce race to lead in artificial intelligence, which can power robots, self-driving cars, and smart assistants.
In recent years, the U.S. has banned exports of some advanced computer chips to China, saying the technology could be used for military purposes.
Xi Jinping (China’s president since 2013) wants China to make its own AI and share it with other countries, while the U.S. worries about losing its edge.
Article_Structure: WHO: Xi Jinping and Chinese AI companies like Moonshot and DeepSeek
WHAT: Xi says AI development should be shared globally, not kept by one country, and announces China’s plans to help other nations
WHERE: At the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai
WHY: Because China wants to challenge U.S. dominance in AI and show it is a fair global leader

perspectives.description: China’s offer of free AI training and weather tools can help poorer countries gain skills and technology they couldn't afford alone.
The United States sees China’s AI push as a security risk, worried that shared technology could be used to spy or build weapons.
No matter who leads, the spread of AI is happening fast, and global rules are still being written.
